clue.text: From fire, save old instrument

parts.note: to fire someone from a job is to sack them
save in the sense of except, which is but

explanation.surface: A plea to rescue a valuable antique from a burning building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From fire' reads as out of the flames, but 'fire' is the dismissal sense. A SACKBUT is an early form of trombone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance brass instrument, forerunner of the trombone.

clue.text: Given men, turn round defeats after change of heart

indicators.note: turn round tells us to read the altered word backwards from end to start
the heart of a seven-letter word is its middle letter, and that letter is swapped for another

explanation.surface: A team, newly reinforced with players, reverses its run of losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after change of heart' turns the middle E of DEFEATS into F, giving DEFFATS; 'turn round' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A workplace that is staffed has been supplied with its workers, so it has been given men.

clue.text: Where one's effortlessly taken up skiing?

definitions.text: Where one's effortlessly taken up skiing?

parts.words: Where one's effortlessly taken up skiing?
parts.note: taking up a sport without effort is the false reading; really it is being carried uphill on a seat at a ski resort

explanation.surface: Someone who picked up skiing with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' looks like starting a hobby, but here it means literally carried up the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-resort lift with suspended seats carries skiers up the mountain with no effort on their part.

clue.text: Complain sheepishly of money invested in stretch of fishing

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a beat is a stretch of river where an angler has fishing rights
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: An angler grumbles timidly about the cost of a fishing beat.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEAT is a stretch of river let out to anglers; L (pound) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is a sheep's cry, and to bleat is also to whine or complain feebly.

clue.text: Islander Stan went mad with suppressed frenzy

indicators.note: suppressed means held down inside, so one piece is kept within the other
a word that goes mad loses its order, so these four letters are rearranged

parts.note: mania is a state of frenzy

explanation.surface: A man called Stan lost his temper but kept his fury bottled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Islander' is the whole definition; 'went mad' scrambles the name, and 'suppressed' keeps the frenzy held inside that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tasmania, the island state south of mainland Australia, is an islander.

clue.text: Job given to graduate with good string of letters

parts.note: a post is a job or position
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A new graduate lands a job and receives a pile of congratulatory mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the batch of letters received, especially by a newspaper or broadcaster.

clue.text: Cut back fruit

definitions.meaning: a dried plum is a fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Pruning means trimming plants or costs, and a dried plum carries the same name.

clue.text: Team is very keen for growth, naturally, not being on top

definitions.text: growth, naturally, not being on top

parts.note: a side is a team
someone who burns for something is very keen on it

explanation.surface: A sports team yearns for growth, if only it weren't top of the league already.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes hair that grows down the cheeks rather than on top of the head; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are strips of whisker grown at the sides of the face, natural hair that is not on the crown.

clue.text: Fish in black stream

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in a dark brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The brill is a flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: With locks unpinned, one may be a stunner

definitions.text: With locks unpinned, one may be a stunner

parts.words: With locks unpinned, one may be a stunner
parts.note: the surface suggests a beauty letting down her hair; really a bomb whose pin is pulled, and a stun version exists

explanation.surface: A woman lets her hair down and turns out to be gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' and 'stunner' suggest hair and beauty, but the pin is the safety pin pulled before a stun device is thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is armed by pulling its pin, and stun versions disable without killing.

clue.text: An entrance of stone

parts.note: an gives the article A
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A doorway built from stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Healthy snack providing newsworthy quote

parts.note: sound means healthy, as in sound of body
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: A nutritious snack that makes a good headline.
explanation.definitionFit: A short extract of speech chosen for broadcast because it is catchy is this kind of quote.

clue.text: Preliminary objective attained using bare fists

indicators.note: using these letters means working them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boxer achieves an early goal fighting without gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the initial bag reached is the first goal, and idiomatically it is an initial stage achieved.

clue.text: Knocked over a plank of wood

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the letters are read backwards in this down-the-page sense

parts.note: a slab is a thick flat piece, like a plank

explanation.surface: Someone tips over a board of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked over' reverses A SLAB as a whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree.

clue.text: Wander off train of thought

definitions.meaning: the ... of an argument is its general meaning or tenor

explanation.definitionFit: Floating aimlessly away is one sense; the general gist of what someone says is another.

clue.text: Avoid direct speaking, but be persuasive

definitions.meaning: to ... a subject is to skirt it without addressing it
to talk someone round is to persuade them

explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Circling a topic in conversation and winning someone over by argument share this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Peruvian sailors had meal in a body

parts.note: the Inca were the ancient people of Peru
RN is the Royal Navy, the British navy
to have a meal is to eat, so ate

explanation.surface: Peruvian sailors dined together as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a body' looks like 'all together', but it is the definition: given bodily form.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made flesh, embodied in human form, is described this way.

clue.text: Reduce one's vocal support? That's miserable

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of support
to reduce is to make less

explanation.surface: Fans who stop cheering for their team look gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads 'cheer less' literally: one's vocal support reduced; 'That's' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking joy or comfort, a gloomy place or person is miserable.

clue.text: Bother over quota of worship

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: Fuss about the share of time allotted to prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and reverence, as in religious worship.

clue.text: Favourite you finally stab in pique

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word you

parts.note: to lance is to pierce or stab

explanation.surface: In a fit of resentment, someone at last stabs their favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky ill temper, much like a fit of pique.

clue.text: Do well as stage magician, but finally dropping ring

indicators.note: finally dropping means the letter is lost from the end of the word

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A conjuror thrives on stage until finally losing grip of his ring.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSPERO is the sorcerer of The Tempest; the stage is the theatre, not a conjuring show.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or succeed.

clue.text: Make fun of wolf

definitions.meaning: to ... at something is to mock it
to wolf food is to gobble it

explanation.definitionFit: Jeering at something and eating greedily both go by this verb.

clue.text: State in which nothing prevents you from damming river up

definitions.text: State in which nothing prevents you

indicators.note: a dam holds water back, so the first word is placed around the river
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Nothing can stop you building a dam upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the river's name over in this down entry, and 'damming' puts the word 'from' around it like a dam across a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is the condition of being unconstrained, with nothing holding you back.

clue.text: Instruct British to withdraw from frontier

indicators.note: withdrawing from something means leaving it, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: a border is a frontier

explanation.surface: An order telling British forces to pull back from the border.
explanation.definitionFit: To order someone is to command or instruct them.

clue.text: Fantasy that barrier can stop troops

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the troops sit inside the barrier

parts.note: a dam is a barrier
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: The fantasy that a wall could halt an invading army.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a fantasy or vision of something hoped for.

clue.text: Percentage growth resulting from Labour efforts?

definitions.text: Percentage growth resulting from Labour efforts?

parts.words: Percentage growth resulting from Labour efforts?
parts.note: looks like a political party's economic record, but labour is childbirth and the growth is in population

explanation.surface: A boast about economic growth under a Labour government.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour, capitalised as the British political party, here means giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of live births per thousand people is a measure of population growth.

clue.text: Farm building with room for one child

indicators.note: having room for something means holding it inside

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A barn with space for a single child.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.

clue.text: Dislike including son in expedition

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to hate is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: Resenting having to take one's son on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey, but it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its old sense means promptness or speed, as in 'with all expedition'.

clue.text: Pride being linked to this old title

definitions.text: Pride being linked to this old title

parts.words: Pride being linked to this old title
parts.note: the old title is a Jane Austen novel whose name joins pride to a second noun with 'and'

explanation.surface: Arrogance associated with an ancient aristocratic rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old title' suggests a noble rank, but it is the title of an 1813 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel pairs pride with bias in its title.

clue.text: Thrown, when horse did this?

definitions.meaning: a startled horse that rears or jumps aside is said to shy

explanation.definitionFit: Tossed is one sense; a horse starting back in fright is the other.

clue.text: Holding a potty, sprinted fast

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, and to sprint is to run fast
potty is informal for mad

explanation.surface: A runner dashing along while clutching a child's potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like quick, matching 'sprinted', but it means abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month of fasting from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Major bone, in total, bird has broken

indicators.note: breaking into something puts a piece inside it

parts.note: a sum is a total
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird has fractured one of its major bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is a large flat bone in the centre of the chest.
